selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the Fourth Truth?
questions.answer: All created things point to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Why are the many shared features of created things important in this proof?
questions.answer: Shared features show a common source.

questions.question: Why is it important that many beings are present together at the same time?
questions.answer: It shows they belong to one organized creation.

questions.question: What does it mean that some things are like small copies or larger versions of others?
questions.answer: It means the same design can be seen at different sizes, which points to one Designer.

questions.question: What does it suggest when a small thing and a large thing carry a similar design?
questions.answer: It suggests one Designer made both.

questions.question: How do general classes and single members work together in this proof?
questions.answer: Both the group and the member reflect the same divine design.

questions.question: How do creatures help and complete one another?
questions.answer: They support each other in the jobs they were created to do.

questions.question: What does mutual support among creatures tell us about the world?
questions.answer: It tells us the world is arranged with order and purpose.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the cosmos as a whole?
questions.answer: It says the cosmos is a unified whole, not something broken into separate rule.

questions.question: What truth about Allah is being explained in this passage?
questions.answer: The passage explains Allah’s unity.

questions.question: Does the passage present only one proof or many signs for this truth?
questions.answer: It presents many signs.

questions.question: How can things be joined in one world but still remain unique?
questions.answer: They can share one system while each having its own identity.

questions.question: How can both similarity and uniqueness point to the same Creator?
questions.answer: Similarity shows one design, and uniqueness shows special knowledge and choice.

questions.question: Why would individual differences also matter?
questions.answer: Because special differences show careful choice and wisdom in creation.

questions.question: What is the lesson from similar built-in traits in many beings?
questions.answer: Their natural traits come from the same Maker.

questions.question: What is meant by the impress of artistry?
questions.answer: It means signs of careful making and beauty can be seen in creation.

questions.question: What does this support between created things say about dominion in the universe?
questions.answer: It says one Lord manages the whole universe.

questions.question: What wrong idea is pushed away by saying the cosmos cannot be fragmented?
questions.answer: The idea that different parts of the universe have different independent rulers.

questions.question: If a student asked, “What does this passage prove about the Maker?” what would be the best short answer?
questions.answer: It proves that the Maker is one.

questions.question: What two things about beings are mentioned together at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: Their existence and their visible appearance.

questions.question: How does resembling one another help prove one Creator?
questions.answer: Similarity shows they were made with one plan and one wisdom.

questions.question: How do repeating patterns across creation support belief in one Lord?
questions.answer: Repeating patterns point to one way of creating and one command.

questions.question: What does it mean when the passage says some things are like mini or larger forms of others?
questions.answer: It means similar designs appear again and again at different sizes.

questions.question: What does the shared artistry in creation show?
questions.answer: It shows one Maker gave beauty, order, and skill to all things.
